Privacy Policy

Effective date: November 19, 2026

Who we are

Yin Hospitality International, LLC ("YHI," "we," "us," or "our") operates CourtCheck, a mobile service for finding pickleball facilities, checking in, and sharing facility conditions. This policy explains how we handle information when you use CourtCheck or contact us about the service.

Account and SMS verification

We collect your mobile phone number and verification status and process account identifiers and session information to create, authenticate, and secure your account. CourtCheck uses one-time SMS codes. Your optional contact email is not used to sign in.

During onboarding, you select an experience level and confirm that you are at least 18. We record your confirmation and its time. CourtCheck assigns a system-generated username and an account role. You may provide, update, or remove a contact email and update your experience level in Profile.

When you request a code, the app asks you to agree to receive a verification SMS at that number. CourtCheck keeps a separate record of the destination phone number, the time of consent, the disclosure version, the source, and an identifier used to avoid duplicate records on retry. The consent record does not contain the verification code. SMS consent is for authentication only. Message frequency depends on your requests, and standard message and data rates may apply.

We do not sell, rent, share, or transfer SMS opt-in data or consent to third parties for their own purposes, including marketing. Providers helping us deliver and secure authentication messages may process the information needed to perform that service for us.

Location and directions

You can create an account and browse facilities without granting location permission. CourtCheck requests foreground location when you choose to check in or tap Use My Location.

  • Check In. The app requests a current, high-accuracy location and sends latitude, longitude, and the facility identifier to the server to verify that you are inside the facility's check-in area. The check-in history record stores the facility and activity timestamps, not the submitted device coordinates. Other players cannot see your coordinates through check-in information.
  • Use My Location. On the player map, the app uses the resulting coordinates to center the map and show your position. This action does not submit a check-in or save your coordinates in the CourtCheck database. Authorized administrators can instead use this action in the facility editor to select a point that can be saved as the public facility location.
  • Maps and directions. The app uses native map services to display maps. The administrator's facility editor can send place queries or selected coordinates to platform search and geocoding services, including Apple MapKit on iOS. When you open Directions, CourtCheck passes the facility's public coordinates or address to Apple Maps or Google Maps. The external maps service handles the starting point, routing, and location permissions under its own privacy policy.

CourtCheck does not continuously track player location or collect it in the background. Check-ins expire on the server after 90 minutes unless ended earlier, such as when you check out or the facility is deactivated.

Facility activity, reports, and feedback

We record your facility, check-in time, expiration time, checkout time, and why the session ended. We use these records to manage active check-ins, show facility activity, and calculate play-time summaries and rankings. Your personal play-time summary is available in your Profile.

Signed-in players can see facility activity counts and the system-generated usernames and experience levels of checked-in players. A facility's monthly leaderboard can also show usernames, experience levels, ranks, and time played there. These views do not show contact information. A system-generated username limits how you are identified to other players, but your account and activity can be associated within CourtCheck while your account is active.

If you submit a preset facility-status report, we record its type, facility, timing, and account association. Players see aggregate reports and reporter counts, not reporter identities. If you send a correction or suggest a park through Are we missing something?, we store your message, category, relevant facility information, and review status. Authorized administrators can review the message and its associated username while that association exists. Please only include information needed to explain the issue.

Authorized administrators manage facilities and check-in areas, review feedback, and may access account or activity records through role-restricted tools or database permissions as needed to operate and protect CourtCheck. We also process information you choose to provide when you email support.

How we use and share information

We use information to operate and secure accounts, deliver verification codes, verify check-ins, display facility activity, maintain facility information, respond to feedback and support requests, prevent misuse, and comply with legal obligations.

  • Service providers. Supabase provides authentication, database, server functions, and Realtime updates. Twilio delivers verification SMS through Supabase Auth. We require providers acting on our behalf to protect the information they process for us consistently with this policy and to use it for the services they provide to us.
  • Technical operations. Our service and its providers may process technical information such as IP addresses, request times, authentication events, SMS delivery information, and diagnostics to deliver, maintain, and protect the service.
  • Other disclosures. We may disclose information at your direction or when reasonably necessary to comply with law, respond to lawful requests, investigate fraud or abuse, protect people or the service, or transfer operations as part of a business transaction, subject to applicable law and this policy.

CourtCheck does not sell or rent personal information, use it for behavioral advertising, or use advertising or analytics SDKs in the app.

Account deletion and retention

Players can request permanent deletion in Profile → Delete Account. Administrators can also use Delete Account on the administrator home screen. Confirming a successful request deletes your authentication account, profile (including your username and optional email), and role membership and signs you out.

Current check-ins and status reports are closed or ended. Historical check-in and status records are retained without their direct link to your account. Facility feedback can remain, including text you entered, but its direct link to your profile is removed. The contents of a message may still identify you if you included identifying details. Facility records can remain, and administrator attribution linked to your account is removed. Separate SMS consent records, including the destination phone number, are not automatically deleted with your account.

We keep information as reasonably necessary to operate and secure the service, maintain legitimate operational or consent records, comply with legal obligations, and resolve disputes. Retention depends on the type of record and the reason it is kept. Limited copies may also be retained in backups or provider records subject to applicable operational and legal requirements. Contact us if you need help deleting an account or have questions about what may remain.

Security, choices, and privacy rights

CourtCheck uses access controls and restricts administrative functions and private records through server-side permissions. Keep your device, phone number, and verification codes secure.

You may change or clear your contact email, update your experience level, and control foreground location access through your device settings. Turning off location access stops location-verified check-ins but still allows facility browsing. You can manually end an active check-in or delete your account through the app.

Depending on applicable law, you may have rights to access, correct, or delete personal information, obtain a copy, or exercise other privacy choices. Email us to make a request. We may verify your identity and apply exceptions permitted or required by law.

Age eligibility

CourtCheck is intended for adults who are at least 18 years old. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. Contact us if you believe someone under 18 provided personal information, so we can investigate and take appropriate action.

Changes and contact

We may update this policy as our practices or legal requirements change. We will update the effective date and provide additional notice when required.
